name: Mexico La Laja Honey, Tlaltetela, Veracruz
origin: Mexico, Tlaltetela, Veracruz (La Laja, family farm since 1920)
process: Honey (pulp kept through fermentation, dried up to 20 days on raised beds)
vendor_notes: Supremely sweet with a mild orange citric acidity and a smooth, creamy body; very clean and consistent. Sweetness 7/7, brightness 6/7, body 5/7. Grown 1,130-1,250 m.
goal: Light-medium roast: big sweetness and creamy body with soft orange
rationale: Lower-grown (1,130-1,250 m) Caturra/Garnica, so softer, less dense beans, and honey processing leaves fruit sugars on them: they brown fast and can scorch or tip. So it charges cooler (183 C) on a gentler burner, with more air after dry end for chaff. Its strength is sweetness (7/7) and body rather than sharp acidity, which suits a light-medium finish: ~12 C after first crack, DTR ~21%. FC 187 C is set from the 18 Rabbit honey, which cracked at 188.9-189.4 C on this roaster; softer beans may go a degree lower.
steps: Preheat to 183 C, then hold steady 10+ min (BT/ET flat).
Charge 170 g at BT 183. Burner 68%, air 30, drum 90.
TP ~0:36 near 108 C. RoR is highest here, then falls.
At 176 C (~6:07): burner 44%. RoR ~10 and falling.
FC ~7:20 at ~187 C: burner 40%, air 55. Then 36%.
Drop ~9:15 at ~199 C (12 C after FC).

rest.note: Honey-processed and light-medium: drinkable after 5 days, sweetest around a week.

history.note: Initial light-to-medium plan from the Coffee Bean Corral page, using the measured opening on this roaster (TP ~0:36 at ~110 C) and FC 187 C (18 Rabbit honey: 188.9-189.4 C) from the Honduras and PNG roasts.
